channel.title: Agrippa on Anti-Federalist Library
channel.description: Recent content in Agrippa on Anti-Federalist Library

item.title: Agrippa I
item.description: Warns that concentrating federal authority will erode local representation and threaten liberty.

item.title: Agrippa II
item.description: Argues that a large republic cannot effectively represent diverse communities or protect individual interests.

item.title: Agrippa III
item.description: Rejects the need for a new constitution, claiming that existing state structures are sufficient for governance.

item.title: Agrippa IV
item.description: Criticizes the proposed judiciary for granting the federal government dominance over state legal systems.

item.title: Agrippa V
item.description: Highlights the absence of a bill of rights as a major flaw, leaving civil liberties unprotected.

item.title: Agrippa VI
item.description: Describes how centralizing power weakens the independence and practical function of state governments.

item.title: Agrippa VII
item.description: Predicts unequal economic burdens under federal tax policies, especially in commercial states like Massachusetts.

item.title: Agrippa VIII
item.description: Raises concerns about federal control of trade enabling monopolies and disadvantaging local producers.

item.title: Agrippa IX
item.description: Flags vague constitutional language as a gateway for federal overreach and abuse of power.

item.title: Agrippa X
item.description: Calls for reforming the Articles of Confederation rather than adopting an untested central framework.

item.title: Agrippa XI
item.description: Urges rejection of the Constitution, warning that its adoption risks undermining both liberty and state autonomy.
